summary:
Jonathan Davis sustained a catastrophic crush injury to his left arm when it became entrapped in an industrial metal stamping press at his workplace. He presented to the emergency department in traumatic shock with a mangled, unsalvageable upper extremity and complete vascular and neurologic disruption. Imaging confirmed extensive comminuted fractures and cessation of arterial blood flow.

An emergency above-elbow amputation was performed, with removal of the arm between shoulder and elbow. Following a seven-day hospitalization marked by appropriate pain management and wound healing, the patient was discharged to outpatient care.

The postoperative course was complicated by severe phantom limb pain and development of a traumatic neuroma at the nerve stump, which interfered with prosthetic fitting. A revision procedure excised the neuroma and transposed the nerve endings into muscle tissue to mitigate pain.

After insurance authorization delays, the patient received a custom myoelectric prosthesis and underwent an extended rehabilitation program spanning over a year. Through physical therapy, he achieved independent operation of the prosthetic arm, restored shoulder range of motion, and regained functional capacity including activities of daily living and driving. He recently completed therapy with demonstrated ability to perform fine motor tasks and carry moderate loads. The patient is now cleared to return to modified work duties at his facility.
